content.title: The Biggest Manicure Color For Spring 2026 Is A Pastel Millennial Throwback You Either Loved Or Hated
content.text: Published on April 10, 2026 0 seconds of 15 secondsVolume 0%This ad will end in 1400:0100:1300:15 How to Make Jar Vinaigrette Credit: Getty Images/Jeremy Moeller After a winter of burgundy and navy manicures, spring steps in at just the right time with an opportunity to be more fun with your nails. Shades like coral red, baby pink, and even butter yellow are lined up ready to grace your fingers each month, and spring 2026 is giving an "out-of-style" color new life. Mint isn't just for your iced tea this season, but your nails too, whether you're scarred from early 2000s pastel mint chevron print or unironically miss it. Mint nails are taking over salons, and they’re perfect for spring. OPI That's Hula-rious. Credit: Courtesy OPI Mint Nails Are the Manicure of Spring Mint was a popular color in fashion and beauty during the early 2000s, when we are all donning chevron-print dresses and popped-collar polos. The in-between teal-aqua color hasn't been seen much since—to many people's relief—until it just started reappearing in fashion shows and nail collections. Pastels always make a flattering choice for spring, since they’re not only vibrant and fresh, but also complement your springtime occasions—including Easter, Mother's Day, and more—and wardrobe. While mint has been a less popular choice at the nail salon than classic baby blue, it's popping up amongst other unexpected shades, such as melon orange and butter yellow, as a top color choice for spring and summer nails. Essie Mint Candy Apple. Credit: Essie How To Choose Mint nails are meant to be a vibrant pastel—creamy, opaque, and with enough pigment not to veer too white. It’s softer than royal blue, but slightly deeper and more green-toned than baby blue. It captures a certain retro feel, like the pastel containers your grandma would pack leftovers into, or the iconic Clinique foundation bottle, or the Tiffany's box your 2000s heart necklace came packaged in. It's Between Blue and Green The good news is that you're only really at risk of choosing something less mint and more baby blue, and it would still be a flattering mani. A better bet is arriving to the salon knowing the best mint nail colors to ask for. Essie’s Mint Candy Apple captures that creamy green-blue finish, while Essie's Turquoise and Caicos veers more sage-esque in color. OPI’s creamy That's Hula-rious also captures that perfect green-forward tint with a hint of aqua. Consider Adding a Chrome Top Coat A fun seasonal variation of mint nails would be topping it all off with a chrome top coat for an even shinier, luminescent finish. Chrome top coats are often complementary with pastel colors and tend to lighten the appearance of the base polish just a bit, which might be ideal for those worried about the chosen mint nail color looking too bright.
